title: The broker
description: The loop from a root asking for work to a child reporting that the work is done. These are the routes every agent session on this machine is dispatched, briefed, watched, collected and acknowledged through. The inventory's own body is assembled in the application rather than generated here, because the 409 that refuses a stale receipt carries the whole 200 body inside its error object and the two have to be the same bytes.

BrokerDispatchRequest.description: The whole body of POST /v1/orchestrator/tasks. The brief is not in it: a caller writes <task_root>/<task_id>/task.json first, and this names it. The secret travels one way — it is never returned, and the child receives it in the one line typed into its composer.

secret.description: 64 lowercase hex characters, the caller's own. Only its SHA-256 is stored.

inventory_generation.description: The receipt from the inventory this dispatch was decided from. Absent is refused: a dispatch that read nothing cannot have been arbitrated against what is already running.

BrokerWarning.description: Something the dispatcher should know that did not stop the work. A warning is never a refusal — by the time one is written the task is recorded and its tab is opening.

BrokerRoot.description: The session a task was dispatched by. `poll_only` is carried even when false: a reader that has to infer it cannot tell an attended root from one that was never recorded.

BrokerWorktree.description: The isolated checkout a task was given. `base` is recorded once and never recomputed: a reader asking whether this branch produced anything compares head against it, and recomputing would answer against a tree that has moved.

commits.description: Commits the branch carries over its base, or null when git could not be asked. Unknown is never permission to dispose of anything.

BrokerLanding.description: What became of a delivery. Delivered is not reviewed and reviewed is not landed; `landed` is the one rung a caller cannot assert on its own word, because the broker proves it by asking git for ancestry.

BrokerNoticeState.description: Where the completion notice has got to. `delivered` means bytes reached a composer, which is not observation — only `acknowledged` stops the resend.

BrokerNotice.description: The durable envelope for telling a root its child finished. It is a ledger rather than a flag because what it records is a promise to somebody who is not here.

BrokerVerification.description: A child's own account of what it ran. It is the child speaking, not a measurement this daemon made.

BrokerResult.description: What a child wrote about itself. The secret it authenticated with is never carried here.

BrokerTask.description: One dispatched piece of work, as the console and a dispatching root read it.

permission.description: The ceiling the dispatch asked for; `full` when task.json said nothing.

timeout_minutes.description: The task's whole budget, on the wall clock, counted from `created` — when the dispatch was admitted, not when the child was briefed — with no grace and no pause while the daemon is down. Past it the task is `timeout` whatever it is doing.

claims_declared.description: Whether the dispatch said anything about claims at all. `I declared none` and `I did not say` are different requests, and only one of them can be arbitrated.

declared_writes.description: What the dispatch declared this task would write — its landing write set — fixed at dispatch and never cleared, whatever its lease became. Absent when that cannot be known: nothing was declared, or an isolated task was stored before this field existed by a broker that erased its list.

lease_scope.description: Whether `declared_writes` also reserve those paths against other roots (`shared`: the task writes the shared checkout, and `claims` is that list) or not (`worktree`: it writes its own checkout, and `claims` is empty).

accepted_at.description: When the child signed for its briefing with its own secret — POST …/accepted, or accepted.json. The only proof the briefing was read; a tab that starts a turn proves only that something is running.

verdict.description: The broker's own sentence when it ended a task the child did not (a timeout, a tab that never opened). Never a result: `result` is only ever what the child wrote.

respawn_of.description: The spawn_failed task this one retried.

BrokerDispatchResult.description: The intent committed and a tab was asked for. `replayed` is how a caller tells a fresh dispatch from one it had already made; `warnings` is omitted when empty rather than sent as an empty array, so that `there is nothing to tell you` never looks like a list somebody forgot to fill.

unfinished.description: Unfinished work is never paged: it rides on every page, because a caller reading page two is still answerable for what is running.

BrokerAccepted.description: The answer to POST /complete: the outcome was recorded. Deliberately bare — what the task did belongs in its result, which the broker already holds.

BrokerAckResult.description: `changed` false is a successful second acknowledgement, not a refusal: a caller that is unsure its ACK landed must be able to send it again.

BrokerInflightRow.description: One line of work outstanding in a repository. `visibility` is `live` while the task is running and `unmerged` once it has finished with a branch nobody has taken; settled work is not listed at all. A stored row this daemon cannot decode is `unreadable` in both `visibility` and `state`, with only its id and the columns stored beside the record: it is listed because it is not absent.

from_session.description: The sender, named by its terminal id or by its conversation id: it is describing itself and knows both.

to_session.description: The recipient, named by terminal id only. A message addressed to a conversation would follow it into whichever tab holds it, and the sender meant the tab.

BrokerMessageResult.description: `ok` means the bytes reached a composer. It never means the assistant read them — that is a later fact with its own evidence.

BrokerWhoAmI.description: Which tab a conversation is in. Five fields and no more: what that session is working on is not the broker's to hand to whoever knows a conversation id.

BrokerSessionDelivery.description: A root's own receipt: one sentence saying this turn delivered something. It produces the check that means `delivered, awaiting approval`, and can never produce `landed`.

BrokerRespawnResult.description: POST /v1/orchestrator/tasks/:id/respawn: a spawn_failed task's task.json copied under a fresh id and dispatched. `secret` is the new task's, returned because the caller may not have chosen it; `original_task` is the first task of the respawn family the limit of two is counted over.

BrokerExecutorStatus.description: What the beat last saw of the session running a task. `not_seen` is one complete reading without it; `executor_missing` is two complete readings at least a minute apart in one process epoch, the Swift app's rule; `unknown` is no complete reading yet. An observation, held in memory and never written: only a crossing into or out of `executor_missing` is recorded, as an event.

observed_at.description: The last reading that showed it; absent when none has.

generation.description: The beat's reading number when it was last seen. It moves on every pass while nothing is written, which is the point.

BrokerObservations.description: The beat's in-memory reading of the machine: what it observed rather than what it decided.

deferred_notices.description: Notices waiting, in memory, for a root that was showing a menu or whose terminal was busy.

sources.description: Each source's own completeness in the same reading. `complete` above is their AND; whether one child's tab is gone is asked of the source that owns it.

BrokerLanes.description: The terminal lanes: one writer per terminal, and one machine-wide ceiling on writes held or waiting. A write past the ceiling is refused (429) before anything is typed; `refused` counts those since this process started.

BrokerPolicy.description: This Mac's house rules as the last briefing carried them, counted in characters. Over `limit` the base is cut at a paragraph break and the local file is always kept whole; `near_limit` is true past 90% of `limit`, before anything has to be cut.

BrokerBeat.description: The loop reporting itself. `stalled` is decided from outside the loop — more than three ticks since the last finished pass — because a loop that has stopped cannot say so.

running.description: Whether the daemon started the beat at all.

at.description: When the last pass finished. Absent before the first.

restarts.description: How many times the supervisor recovered the loop after a panic or an unasked exit.

quiet_seconds.description: Seconds since the last finished pass, or since the start before the first.

BrokerPass.description: What the last finished pass did.

unreadable.description: Stored rows the pass could not decode. They are listed by the task list and the inventory; this is the count.

notes_refused.description: progress.json bodies refused for good this pass — too long, empty or not signed by the task — each also one `task.progress.refused` event.

closed.description: Child sessions closed this pass after a spawn_failed verdict, each proved to be the task's own by its pane.

store_error.description: Why the pass could not read the store. A pass that could not read is not a pass that found nothing.

BrokerStoreHealth.description: The store's own account. `writes` counts write transactions that committed something since this process opened the store, and `changes` is SQLite's count of rows this process changed in any table: both stand still while the beat only observes.

BrokerDiagnostics.description: The broker block of /v1/diagnostics: the beat, what its last pass did, the notice ledger, the store, and what the beat has only observed.

BrokerProgressEvent.description: One accepted progress note. `seq` is its row in the store: increasing and never reused, so it is the note's identity on the stream.

BrokerProgressFrame.description: The `orchestrator-progress` event on /v1/events. The first one on a connection carries the newest notes of every live task, so a page that reconnects is level without asking; after that, one per accepted note. A note is never sent twice on one connection.
